title: Put JARVIS on your phone
intro: Very good, sir. Six short steps and I will be in your pocket.

steps.title: Install Tailscale
steps.body: On your iPhone, open the App Store and search for Tailscale. Install it. This is the private tunnel that lets the phone reach this machine; nothing gets exposed to the public internet.
steps.voice: Step one. On your iPhone, install Tailscale from the App Store.

steps.title: Sign in with the same account
steps.body: Open Tailscale and sign in with GitHub as ZyadKamalHamed, the exact account this Mac uses. A different account lands on a different tailnet and the phone will never find me.
steps.voice: Step two. Sign in to Tailscale with GitHub, the same account this Mac uses.

steps.title: Switch the VPN on
steps.body: Flip the toggle at the top of the Tailscale app. iOS will ask permission to add a VPN configuration; approve it. The switch should read Connected.
steps.voice: Step three. Flip the VPN toggle on and approve the configuration prompt.

steps.title: Open the HUD in Safari
steps.body: In Safari, open the address below. Expect the boot screen; give it a second on first load.
steps.voice: Step four. Open the HUD address in Safari. The open button is on your screen.

steps.title: Add to Home Screen
steps.body: Tap the Share button, then Add to Home Screen. You get the arc reactor icon and a full-screen app with no browser chrome.
steps.voice: Step five. Share, then Add to Home Screen.

steps.title: Test it
steps.body: Open JARVIS from the new icon. If the DATA chip in the top rail shows a fresh timestamp, live data is flowing. Remember: the phone needs its Tailscale VPN on, and until the home laptop takes over, this Mac must be awake.
steps.voice: Last step. Open me from the icon and check the data chip is fresh. Then tick this off the board, sir.

outro: Done. I am officially portable, sir.
